paper.title: Robust Thompson Sampling Algorithms Against Reward Poisoning Attacks

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic multi-armed bandit under strong reward poisoning attack
unmapped: The learner knows an upper bound C_bar >= C on the corruption budget (the algorithm's input).
settings.definition_quote: an environment consists of $N$ arms with fixed support in $[0,1]$ reward distributions centered at $\left\{\mu_1, \ldots, \mu_N\right\}$ ... At each round $t$, the attacker observes the arm pulled by the agent $i(t)$, the reward $r^{o}(t)$ ... Then the attacker can inject a perturbation $c(t)$ to the reward ... $C: \sum_{t=1}^T|c(t)| \leq C$

settings.name_in_paper: Linear contextual bandit under strong reward poisoning attack
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t$, $N$ contexts $\{x_{i}(t) \in \mathbb{R}^d\}$ are revealed ... $\mathbb{E}[r(t)|x_{i(t)}(t)]=x_{i(t)}(t)^T \mu$ ... $\left\|x_i(t)\right\|_{2} \leq 1,\|\mu\|_{2} \leq 1$ ... $\epsilon_{t}$ is conditionally $\sigma$-sub-Gaussian ... the agent will receive the corrupted reward ${r}(t)=r^{o}(t)+c(t)$

algorithms.name: Robust Thompson Sampling for Stochastic Bandits (Alg 3)
Robust Thompson Sampling for Contextual Linear Bandits (Alg 4)

symbols.C_bar: robustness hyper-parameter of the algorithm, an upper bound on the corruption budget C

conditions: C_bar >= C (corruption budget at most the algorithm's robustness level)

source.label: thm:gaussian
source.quote: For the $N$-armed stochastic bandit problem under any reward poisoning attack with corruption level $C$, the expected regret of the Robust Thompson Sampling Alg \ref{alg:3} with $\overline{C} \geq C$ is bounded by: $\mathbb{E}[\mathcal{R}(T)] \leq O(\sqrt{N T \ln N} + N\overline{C} + N)$ The big-Oh notation hides only absolute constants.

results.notes: The paper's N (number of arms) is K. Regret is defined through the uncorrupted means. When C is known, setting C_bar = C gives O(sqrt(KT log K) + KC). When C is unknown, the text sets C_bar = sqrt(T ln N/N); this needs T and gives O(sqrt(NT ln N)) when C <= sqrt(T ln N/N), otherwise O(T). That case is only a remark and is not recorded separately. The algorithm itself does not use T, so the horizon is recorded as anytime.

bound.expression: d*exp((1 + C*gamma_r/sqrt(d))**2)*sqrt(d*T*log(T)*log(T/delta)) + C*gamma_r*exp((1 + C*gamma_r/sqrt(d))**2)*sqrt(d*T*log(T)) + d**2*exp((1 + C*gamma_r/sqrt(d))**2)/gamma_r*log(T)*sqrt(log(T/delta)) + C*d*exp((1 + C*gamma_r/sqrt(d))**2)*log(T)
bound.expression_latex: O\left( d e^{(1 + \frac{C\gamma}{\sqrt{d}})^2} \sqrt{d T \ln T \ln \left(\frac{T}{\delta}\right)} + C\gamma e^{(1 + \frac{C\gamma}{\sqrt{d}})^2} \sqrt{ d T \ln T} + \frac{d^2 e^{(1 + \frac{C\gamma}{\sqrt{d}})^2}}{\gamma} \ln T \sqrt{\ln \left(\frac{T}{\delta}\right)} + Cd e^{(1 + \frac{C\gamma}{\sqrt{d}})^2} \ln T \right)

symbols.gamma_r: robustness hyper-parameter gamma > 0 of the weighted ridge estimator (weights w_t = min{1, gamma/||x||_{B^{-1}}})

source.label: thm:context
source.quote: For the stochastic contextual bandit problem with linear payoff functions, with probability $1-\delta$, the total regret in time $T$ for Robust Thompson Sampling for Contextual Linear Bandits (Algorithm \ref{alg:4}) is bounded by $O( d e^{(1 + \frac{C\gamma}{\sqrt{d}})^2} \sqrt{d T \ln T \ln (\frac{T}{\delta})} + C\gamma e^{...} \sqrt{ d T \ln T} + \frac{d^2 e^{...}}{\gamma} \ln T \sqrt{\ln (\frac{T}{\delta})} + Cd e^{...} \ln T )$

results.notes: In the text, gamma = sqrt(d)/C (C known) gives O(d sqrt(dT ln T ln(T/delta)) + C d sqrt(d) ln T sqrt(ln(T/delta))). gamma = sqrt(d/T) (C unknown) gives O~(d sqrt(dT)) when C <= sqrt(T). These are remarks, not recorded separately. Contexts are revealed by the environment with no stated distribution, so they are treated as adversarial. The algorithm uses sigma and delta through v_t.
